newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: SOUTH KOREA TO SUPPLY $300 MLN TO MERCHANT BANKS.
newsitem.headline: SOUTH KOREA TO SUPPLY $300 MLN TO MERCHANT BANKS.

text.p: South Korea said on Thursday it was considering supplying $300 million in loans to merchant banks to ease their financial difficulties.

The finance ministry said it was reviewing a plan to funnel $300 million out of $1 billion in emergency loans the Bank of Korea released to commercial banks on Tuesday into the secondary banking institutions.
On Wednesday, the central bank said it had supplied $1 billion to seven commercial banks to ease dollar shortages.
A ministry official said of the total, $300 million had yet to be delivered.
Merchant banks faced tightening liquidity after the troubled Kia Group was put under creditors' protection in July.
The protection will continue until the end of September.
The group is known to owe the nation's merchant banks about 3.9 trillion won.
Bankers said overseas financing by domestic banks had become more difficult as a series of corporate failures had damaged the credit ratings of South Korean companies and financial insititutions.
